csv_project_name: DB for SMF Consolidated Rental Car Center
csv_scope_of_work: The County of Sacramento (County) owns and operates the Sacramento International Airport (Airport or SMF) through the Department of Airports (Department). SMF is a commercial service airport located 12 miles from downtown Sacramento. SMF opened in 1967 under its previous name Sacramento Metropolitan Airport, and in the 1990s was renamed Sacramento International Airport. Currently, SMF is best known as the gateway between Northern California destinations and major cities across the United States and the world. Terminal B, Concourse B, and the Automated People Mover (APM) system opened in 2011 as part of a major County capital project called The Big Build.
csv_disciplines_requested: Architecture Services, Design Build/Developer, Civil Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Structural Engineering

title: Design-Build for SMF Consolidated Rental Car Center
short_description: Design-build procurement for a major consolidated rental car center at Sacramento International Airport.
project_location: Sacramento International Airport, Sacramento, California, USA
project_scope: Design-build project for a consolidated rental car center (ConRAC) at Sacramento International Airport (SMF), a commercial airport about 12 miles from downtown Sacramento. The tender indicates a major airport landside transportation facility funded in part through the FAA Airport Improvement Program. No gross floor area, number of levels, structural spans, or detailed technical parameters are stated in the source.
services: Design-build/developer services with requested disciplines including architecture, civil engineering, geotechnical engineering, mechanical engineering, and structural engineering.
relevance_explanation:
- Large-scale project with stated construction cost of USD 390–500 million.
- Includes structural engineering within a multidisciplinary design-build team.
- Airport ConRAC buildings can involve long-span parking and circulation structures, but no specific structural complexity is described.
- Primarily a building/transportation facility rather than a bridge or special lightweight structure.
- Design-build format may offer strategic teaming opportunities, but architecture and general building scope dominate.
construction_cost_explanation: Estimated from the tender documents, which state a total construction cost range of USD 390.0M–500.0M; midpoint used.
fee_explanation: No explicit design fee is stated. Useful basis: total construction cost is given as USD 390.0M–500.0M, and the procurement is design-build for a large airport rental car center involving architecture, civil, geotechnical, mechanical, and structural engineering.
references_qualifications: Design-build team sought with capabilities in architecture, civil engineering, geotechnical engineering, mechanical engineering, and structural engineering. Mandatory pre-submittal conference attendance is required. DBE participation goal: 5%. No detailed minimum reference counts or project-specific qualification thresholds are stated in the source.
